# dsh-gigaam-stt
**Local Russian speech-to-text for the DeepSeek Harness chat.** Dictate Russian, get Cyrillic text —

with
capitalisation and punctuation — transcribed on your CPU, offline, with no API keys and no clo
italisation and punctuation — transcribed on your CPU, offline, with no API keys and no cloud calls.

The engine is GigaAM v3 (220M Conformer, MIT) exported to ONNX
(`e2e_ctc`, int8) and run by sherpa-o

nnx. The plugin plugs into DSH's
existing voice-input pipeline: it registers a `speechToText` provid

er, so the microphone button in the chat
composer starts working with Russian.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## Features
- **Russian only, properly.** Per ai-sage's benchmark, GigaAM v3 reports ~8.4 % WER on Russian again

st ~19 % for
T-One and ~25 % for Whisper-large-v3 — and its `e2e` variants emit capitalisation and p

unctuation directly.
- **CPU-first and small.** 320 MB int8 model, ~420 MB RSS while loaded, ~0.04 R

TF — 11 s of speech is transcribed
in about 0.45 s on four threads.
- **Lazy and self-cleaning.** Th

e model downloads on first use, loads on first recording (~1 s), unloads after five
idle minutes. No

thing runs in the background.
- **No dependencies.** The plugin itself imports only Node built-ins;

sherpa-onnx is reused from your DSH
installation. No build step, no native compilation, no Python.
-
**Long recordings work.** Audio is cut into pause-aligned windows of 20 s before decoding: a single

pass over
anything past ~200 s aborts sherpa-onnx (5 000 encoder frames), while pause-aligned windo

ws keep memory at
~520 MB and stay within the model's trained length. 214 s of audio decodes in 8.7

s.
- **Numbers as digits.** "двадцать пять" → "25", "в две тысячи двадцать пятом году" → "в 2025 год

у". Conservative:
single words below two stay as words, so "ни один" and "один в один" survive. Swit

ch off with `numbers: words`.
- **Non-blocking.** Recognition runs in a `worker_threads` worker, so

the chat never stalls while decoding.
- **Safe downloads.** Pinned URL, size and SHA-256 for every a
sset; interrupted downloads resume from `.part` files.
## Requirements

- DeepSeek Harness with the voice-input stack — `@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-voice-input-bundle`
(
speech service, mic UI and Remote API). It ships with DSH's experimental voice input; without it thi

s bundle
installs but has no microphone to attach to.
- Node.js 22+ (DSH itself needs a modern Node)

, x86-64 or arm64 Linux/macOS/Windows.
- ~350 MB free disk for the model, ~450 MB RAM while it is lo

aded.
- A browser with microphone access to `DSH Web` (the mic permission prompt appears on first re
browser with microphone access to `DSH Web` (the mic permission prompt appears on first recording).
## Install
Ask your DSH agent to install the bundle, or use the Plugin Manager panel in the DSH Web UI — the in

stall target
accepts any spec `pnpm` accepts:
| Source | Install target |

| npm registry | `dsh-gigaam-stt` |
| GitHub repository | `github:OldSchool686/dsh-gigaam-stt` |
| L

ocal checkout | absolute path, e.g. `/home/me/dsh-gigaam-stt` |
| Tarball | `/home/me/dsh-gigaam-stt

| absolute path, e.g. `/home/me/dsh-gigaam-stt` |
| Tarball | `/home/me/dsh-gigaam-stt-1.1.0.tgz` |
The bundle's patch does three things: it makes `gigaam-local` the default speech provider with langu

age `ru`,
disables the bundled SenseVoice provider (its languages are zh/en/yue/ja/ko, so it would o

nly add noise), and mounts
this provider with `dataRoot: !!js dshHomePath('speech-to-text', 'gigaam'

add noise), and mounts
this provider with `dataRoot: !!js dshHomePath('speech-to-text', 'gigaam')`.
If your profile has no voice-input bundle, the two row overrides are reported as warnings and skippe

d — install
`@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-voice-input-bundle` first, then re-apply this bundle.
## First run
Press the microphone button in the chat composer. The preparation card shows a one-time download of

two files
(~320 MB) from Hugging Face, verified by SHA-256, and the state changes `downloading → loa
0 MB) from Hugging Face, verified by SHA-256, and the state changes `downloading → loading → ready`.
Assets are stored in `~/.dsh/speech-to-text/gigaam/`:
| File | Bytes | SHA-256 |
| `gigaam_v3_e2e_ctc_int8.onnx` | 319869121 | `0aacb41f70f0f5aaac4b45dd430337b9e16b180f22c72af04db85

16e7609c3c0` |
| `gigaam_v3_e2e_ctc_tokens.txt` | 2006 | `f8eb9b115e2748db9c40a5897cae11dd0678cc0b40
[该节后续省略]
## How it works
1. The DSH speech service validates that the recording is a canonical 16 kHz mono PCM16 WAV and hand

s the bytes to
the provider.
2. The provider serialises requests, wakes the worker if needed, and tr

ansfers the audio buffer.
3. The worker strips the 44-byte WAV header, converts PCM16 to float32, an

d splits the speech into windows of at
most `maxSegmentSeconds`, cutting inside pauses (adaptive RMS

threshold over 10 ms frames) and dropping leading and
trailing silence. Each window goes through `O

fflineRecognizer` with `modelConfig.nemoCtc` (GigaAM `e2e_ctc` emits
punctuation and casing directly

).
4. Windows are joined, number words are normalised (unless `numbers: words`), and the text comes

back with
`audioSeconds` and `inferenceSeconds`; the model unloads after the idle timeout.
Measured on an 8-vCPU box (Node 24, int8, 4 threads): model load 0.84 s, decode 0.44–0.46 s for 11.2

9 s of audio,
RTF ~0.043 for long input (214 s in 8.7 s), RSS ~420 MB with the model resident and ~5

20 MB during a long
transcription. One pass over 214 s without windowing used ~2 GB and aborted the

ring a long
transcription. One pass over 214 s without windowing used ~2 GB and aborted the process.
## Privacy
- **No credentials.** The plugin reads one environment variable, `GIGAAM_SHERPA_PATH` (a local files

ystem path). It
never touches DSH credentials, API keys, cookies or the settings store.
- **No telem

etry**, no analytics, no update checks, no accounts.
- **The only network access** is the one-time m

odel download over HTTPS from `modelOrigins`: a plain GET with no
authorization header. It can be sk

ipped entirely by pre-seeding `dataRoot`.
- **Audio never leaves the machine.** The recording goes t

o a local worker thread, is decoded on the CPU, and is
dropped afterwards.
- **Nothing is written ou
tside `dataRoot`** (plus `.part` files inside it while a download is in progress).
